questions.question: What is a Single Left Rotation applied for in an AVL tree?
options: When a left child's left subtree causes imbalance
When a right child's right subtree causes imbalance
To prevent BST degradation to linear linked lists
To enforce the heap property in a Binary Heap
questions.explanation: Single Left Rotation is applied when a left child's left subtree causes imbalance (evidence [1])

questions.question: Why does building a binary heap from an unsorted array of n elements using `buildHeap` cost O(n) time instead of O(n log n)?
options: Because the heap property is enforced in O(n) time
Because the heap property is enforced in O(log n) time
Because the heap property is not enforced at all
Because the heap property is enforced in O(1) time
questions.explanation: Building a binary heap from an unsorted array of n elements costs O(n) time because the heap property is enforced in O(n) time (evidence not explicitly stated but implied from the question context)

questions.question: What is the balance factor of a node in an AVL tree?
questions.explanation: The balance factor of a node in an AVL tree is Height(Left) - Height(Right) (evidence [3])

questions.question: Which traversal order visits BST nodes in ascending sorted sequence?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal visits BST nodes in ascending sorted sequence (evidence [4])

questions.question: What is the property enforced by a Binary Search Tree (BST) for any node X?
options: All keys in the left subtree are greater than or equal to X.key
All keys in the left subtree are strictly smaller than X.key
All keys in the left subtree are strictly greater than X.key
All keys in the left subtree are equal to X.key
questions.explanation: A BST enforces the property that for any node X, all keys in the left subtree are strictly smaller than X.key (evidence [5])

questions.question: What is the worst-case search and insertion time in a degenerate (skewed) BST created by inserting sorted numbers `1, 2, 3, 4, 5`?
questions.explanation: In a degenerate BST, the search and insertion times are O(n) because the tree becomes a linked list.

questions.question: What rotation is applied when a right child's right subtree causes imbalance in an AVL tree?
questions.explanation: A Single Right Rotation (RR) is applied when a right child's right subtree causes imbalance.

questions.question: What is the resulting tree after inserting keys `10, 20, 30` in order into an empty AVL tree?
questions.explanation: Inserting keys in order creates a left-leaning tree, so the resulting tree is [20, 10, 30].

questions.question: Which traversal order is used for node deletion in a BST?
questions.explanation: Post-order traversal is used for node deletion in a BST.

When a right child's right subtree causes imbalance

Used for tree cloning and serialization

questions.question: What is the structural property enforced in a Binary Search Tree (BST)?
options: For any node X, all keys in the left subtree are strictly greater than X.key
For any node X, all keys in the left subtree are strictly smaller than X.key
Inorder traversal of a BST yields elements in sorted descending order
A BST restricts each node to at most three children (left, right, and center)
questions.explanation: For any node X, all keys in the left subtree are strictly smaller than X.key (evidence [2])

questions.question: In a degenerate BST created by inserting sorted numbers `1, 2, 3, 4, 5`, what are the worst-case search and insertion times?
questions.explanation: In a degenerate BST, the tree becomes a linked list, resulting in O(n) search and insertion times (evidence [3])

questions.question: Which traversal order visits BST nodes in ascending sorted sequence?
questions.explanation: In-order visits BST nodes in ascending sorted sequence (evidence [4])

questions.question: What is the height invariant enforced in an AVL Tree?
options: Height difference between left and right subtrees is at most ±1
A BST restricts each node to at most three children (left, right, and center)
questions.explanation: Height difference between left and right subtrees is at most ±1 in an AVL Tree (evidence [5])

questions.question: What is the data structure defined by the provided Python class `BSTNode`?
questions.explanation: The provided class defines a node for a Binary Search Tree (BST), as it restricts each node to at most two children (left and right) and enforces the BST's structural property.

questions.question: What rotation is applied when a right child's right subtree causes imbalance in a BST?
questions.explanation: Single Right Rotation is applied when a right child's right subtree causes imbalance in a BST.

questions.question: What is the property that a BST enforces for any node X?
options: all keys in the left subtree are strictly greater than X.key
all keys in the left subtree are strictly smaller than X.key
all keys in the right subtree are strictly greater than X.key
all keys in the right subtree are strictly smaller than X.key
questions.explanation: For any node X in a BST, all keys in the left subtree are strictly smaller than X.key, and all keys in the right subtree are strictly greater.
